questions.q: What is the null hypothesis of the ADF test?
options: The series has a unit root
why: Correct: ADF assumes a unit root (non-stationary) until the data says otherwise.
This is the KPSS null.
White noise is not the null of either test.
Neither test is about seasons.

questions.q: What is the null hypothesis of the KPSS test?
options: The series has a unit root
why: Correct: KPSS assumes the series is stationary until the data says otherwise.
This is the ADF null.
A trend is not the null of KPSS. With regression='ct' the null is stationarity around a trend.
Neither test checks the distribution.

questions.q: ADF p = 0.62 and KPSS p = 0.01. What do you do?
options: Difference the series and test again
Fit an AR model to the raw series
why: Correct: both tests point to a unit root.
Both tests say the series is not stationary.
A log may help the spread but does not remove a unit root.
AR models need stationary data.

questions.q: ADF p = 0.001 and KPSS p = 0.40. What is the conclusion?
why: Correct: ADF rejects the unit root and KPSS does not reject stationarity.
A unit root needs ADF not to reject.
Mixed signals mean both reject or both fail to reject.
Both tests give clear results here.

questions.q: The ADF statistic is -4.1 and the 5% critical value is -2.87. Do you reject H0 at 5%?
options: Yes, because the value is negative
why: Correct: the statistic is more negative than the critical value, so we reject the unit root.
Being below the critical value means rejection, not the opposite.
Negative values alone mean nothing. The comparison with the critical value matters.
The critical value gives the answer.

questions.q: A model y(t) = 1.0·y(t−1) + ε(t) has what value of phi, and what is the name of the process?
options: phi = 1: random walk with a unit root
why: Correct: phi = 1 gives a random walk, which has a unit root.
AR(1) is stationary only if |phi| < 1.
White noise would have phi = 0, not 1.
This is an autoregressive form, not a moving average.

questions.q: You have only 30 monthly points and ADF gives p = 0.12. What is the best reaction?
options: Be careful: the test has low power on short series. Check the plot, KPSS and ACF
Declare a unit root with certainty
Ignore the test and difference twice
why: Correct: with few points ADF often fails to reject. Use several signals.
Failing to reject does not prove a unit root.
p = 0.12 does not support stationarity.
Differencing twice may over-difference and add noise.
